1000442: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.luminousIntensity_dim_eq_power : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.luminousIntensity.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = PropertyKindCalculus.Dim.power**Luminous intensity reduces to power.** The candela carries the dimension of power, `M·L²·T⁻³` — the scale-spanning reduction (R13).
1000441: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.iso80000_7_dim_one_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = 1**The dimension-one disambiguation, on the standard — the widest in the series.** There exist distinct ISO 80000-7 kinds with the same dimension one — refractive index and emissivity witness it, alongside the efficiencies, efficacies, absorptances, reflectances, transmittances, optical densities, the radiance and luminance factors, the reflectance factor, the chromaticity coordinates, the colour-matching functions, and the photon number. Dimension cannot separate them; the kind layer does.
1000440: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.iso80000_7_dim_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**The scale-spanning collision capstone, on the standard.** There exist distinct ISO 80000-7 kinds with the same dimension `M·L²·T⁻³` — radiant flux and luminous flux witness it (alongside radiant and luminous intensity). The candela reduces to power, so the {dimension functor} cannot separate them; the kind layer — and the unit, `W` versus `lm` — does. This is the dimension-does-not-classify case at its sharpest: the collision is between a base-quantity unit (the candela) and a derived one.
1000439: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.luminousFlux : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseLuminous flux — item 7-13, dimension `M·L²·T⁻³` (unit lm; the photopic partner of radiant flux, the same dimension once the candela reduces to power).
1000438: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.luminousEfficacy : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseLuminous efficacy of radiation `<specified photometric condition>` — item 7-11.1, dimension one (lm/W; luminous flux over radiant flux, the candela reducing to power).
1000437: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.DefiningRelations.luminousEfficacy_dim_from_fluxes : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.luminousEfficacy.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.luminousFlux.dim LTMCTDimensionBase / PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.radiantFlux.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**The luminous efficacy is dimension one because it is a ratio of two fluxes of equal dimension.** Luminous and radiant flux are both `M·L²·T⁻³` (the candela reducing to power, R13), so `K = Φ_v/Φ_e` cancels the dimension — the efficacy's dimensionlessness is a *checked computation from its defining relation*, the photometric analogue of the power factor (IEC 80000-6) and the plane angle (ISO 80000-3). It nonetheless remains a distinct kind from every other dimension-one quantity (see `Part7.iso80000_7_dim_one_collision`).
1000436: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.DefiningRelations.irradianceOf (φ : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.radiantFlux.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) (a : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.area.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.irradiance.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝAn irradiance built as radiant flux / area — classified as an irradiance **by construction** (`E_e = dΦ_e/dA`).
1000435: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.DefiningRelations.irradiance_quot_flux_area : PropertyKindCalculus.QuotientKind (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.radiantFlux.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.area.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.irradiance.kind LTMCTDimensionBase)**Irradiance is radiant flux per area** (item 7-7.1: `E_e = dΦ_e/dA`) — a *cross-part* law, the area an ISO 80000-3 quantity.
1000434: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.radiantFlux : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseRadiant flux, radiant power — item 7-4.1, dimension `M·L²·T⁻³` (unit W).
1000432: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.DefiningRelations.irradianceOf_isQuotient (φ : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.radiantFlux.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) (a : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.area.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity.IsQuotient PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.DefiningRelations.irradiance_quot_flux_area (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part7.DefiningRelations.irradianceOf φ a) φ aThe constructed irradiance satisfies the quotient certificate by construction.
1000431: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.varReactive : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe var **of reactive power** (item 6-60) — *also* `M·L²·T⁻³`, but a unit of reactive power, not active power.
1000430: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.wattActive : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe watt **of active power** (item 6-56) — dimension `M·L²·T⁻³`.
1000429: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.wattActive_varReactive_not_commensurable : ¬PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.wattActive.Commensurable PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.varReactive**The watt of active power and the var of reactive power are not commensurable, though both are `M·L²·T⁻³`.** The standard spends two different unit strings (`W`, `var`) on one dimension precisely to keep the kinds apart — a sharper form of "a dimension does not determine a kind" than Part 5's joule-per-kelvin, where even the unit string agreed.
1000428: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.powerSpecies (id : String) (p : PropertyKindCalculus.ExaminationPrinciple) : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseAn AC power species: dimension `M·L²·T⁻³`, ratio-scale, individuated by its defining construction (examination principle).
1000427: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.iec80000_6_scale_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ (a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase).scale ≠ (b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase).scale**The scale disambiguation, on standard quantities.** There exist distinct IEC 80000-6 kinds with the same dimension `M·L²·T⁻²·C⁻¹` that are separated by *scale type* alone — electric potential (interval, gauge-dependent) and electric potential difference (ratio) witness it. Neither the dimension nor an examination principle tells them apart; the scale layer does. This is requirement R6 on the standard, the electromagnetic counterpart of Part 5's thermodynamic/Celsius temperature.
1000426: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.iec80000_6_dim_one_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = 1**The dimension-1 disambiguation, on standard quantities.** There exist distinct IEC 80000-6 kinds with the same dimension one — relative permittivity and relative permeability witness it (alongside the susceptibilities, the coupling and leakage factors, and the quality, loss, and power factors). Dimension cannot separate them; the kind layer does.
1000425: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.iec80000_6_dim_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**The power collision, on standard quantities.** There exist distinct IEC 80000-6 kinds with the same dimension `M·L²·T⁻³` — active power and reactive power witness it (alongside apparent, complex, and non-active power). PhysLib's `Dimension`, and any dimension-only type system, cannot separate them; the kind layer does — and so do the units, which here even differ in string (`W` vs `var`). This is the electromagnetic dimension-does-not-classify case, sharper than Part 5's joule-per-kelvin.
1000424: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricPotential : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseElectric potential — item 6-11.1, dimension `M·L²·T⁻²·C⁻¹` (unit V), **interval-scale**: fixed only up to an arbitrary additive reference (gauge freedom), so a ratio of electric potentials is not a meaningful operation — only their differences are.
1000423: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricPotential_not_allowsRatio : ¬(PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricPotential.kind LTMCTDimensionBase).scale.AllowsRatio**Electric potential does *not* admit `×`,`÷`.** It is interval-scale (fixed only up to an arbitrary additive reference — gauge freedom), so a ratio of electric potentials is not a meaningful operation — the kind layer refuses it where dimension would not.
1000422: Dimension.charge (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) : Dimension.ExponentThe charge exponent of a `LTMCTDimensionBase` dimension.
1000421: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.capacitance : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseCapacitance — item 6-13, dimension `C²·M⁻¹·L⁻²·T²` (unit F, the farad). The charge/voltage remark is formalized in `Part6.DefiningRelations`.
1000420: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.capacitance_dim_charge : (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.capacitance.dim LTMCTDimensionBase).charge = 2**Capacitance is `C²·M⁻¹·L⁻²·T²`: its charge-exponent is `2`** — the farad carries the charge generator squared (item 6-13).
1000419: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.voltPotential : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe volt **of electric potential** (item 6-11.1) — an *interval-scale* unit.
1000418: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.ampere : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe ampere, the SI unit of electric current (item 6-1).
1000417: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.ampere_voltPotential_not_commensurable : ¬PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.ampere.Commensurable PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.voltPotentialThe ampere and the volt are **not** commensurable — electric current and electric potential are distinct kinds (a type-level fact).
1000416: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.Edge : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty → PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty → PropThis application's system of power quantities — the direct-parent edges among the AC power quantities of the power family (item 6-45).
1000415: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.activePower_reactivePower_comparable : PropertyKindCalculus.MutuallyComparable PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.Edge (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.activePower.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.reactivePower.kind LTMCTDimensionBase)**Mutual comparability is preserved.** Active and reactive power, though distinct kinds, remain *mutually comparable* — they share the super-kind power, so combining them (into the complex power) is possible but only via an explicit up-cast, never silently.
1000414: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.reactivePower : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseReactive power — item 6-60, a power species (the imaginary part of complex power, unit var).
1000413: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.activePower_ne_reactivePower : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.activePower.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.reactivePower.kind LTMCTDimensionBase**Active power and reactive power are distinct kinds — by defining construction, not by fiat.** They have the same dimension `M·L²·T⁻³` and are both "powers", yet they are different kinds *because they isolate different components of the periodic process* (the time-averaged real part vs the imaginary part of the complex power), proved through `distinct_of_examPrinciple` (§7.5) rather than by appealing to their `id` strings. This is the AC-power analogue of width ≠ distance, static ≠ kinetic friction, and Helmholtz ≠ Gibbs energy.
1000412: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.DefiningRelations.resistanceOf (u : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.voltage.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) (i : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricCurrent.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.resistance.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝA resistance built as voltage / current — classified as a resistance **by construction** (Ohm's law `R = U/I`).
1000411: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.DefiningRelations.resistance_quot_voltage_current : PropertyKindCalculus.QuotientKind (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.voltage.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricCurrent.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.resistance.kind LTMCTDimensionBase)**Resistance is voltage per electric current** (Ohm's law, item 6-46: `R = U/I`).
1000410: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricCurrent : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseElectric current — item 6-1, dimension `C·T⁻¹` (unit A). One of the seven ISQ base quantities (taken here over PhysLib's charge generator).
1000408: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.voltage : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseVoltage — item 6-11.3, dimension `M·L²·T⁻²·C⁻¹` (unit V), ratio-scale.
1000406: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.DefiningRelations.resistanceOf_isQuotient (u : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.voltage.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) (i : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.electricCurrent.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) ℝ) : PropertyKindCalculus.Quantity.IsQuotient PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.DefiningRelations.resistance_quot_voltage_current (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.DefiningRelations.resistanceOf u i) u iThe constructed resistance satisfies the quotient certificate by construction.
1000405: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.apparentPower : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseApparent power — item 6-57, a power species (RMS voltage times RMS current, unit VA).
1000404: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.activePower : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseActive power — item 6-56, a power species (the time-averaged real component, unit W).
1000403: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.powerFactor : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBasePower factor — item 6-58, dimension one (active power over apparent power). The remark is formalized in `Part6.DefiningRelations`.
1000402: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.DefiningRelations.powerFactor_dim_from_powers : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.powerFactor.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.activePower.dim LTMCTDimensionBase / PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part6.apparentPower.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**The power factor is dimension one because it is a ratio of two powers.** Active and apparent power are both `M·L²·T⁻³`, so `λ = P/S` cancels the dimension — the power factor's dimensionlessness is a *checked computation from its defining relation*, not a stipulation. (It nonetheless remains a distinct kind from every other dimension-one quantity; see `Part6.iec80000_6_dim_one_collision`.) This is the electromagnetic analogue of the plane angle being a ratio of two lengths and the thermodynamic efficiency being a ratio of two powers.
1000401: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.joule : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe joule, the SI unit of energy (item 5-20.1) — dimension `M·L²·T⁻²`.
1000400: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.kelvin : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe kelvin, the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature (item 5-1).
1000399: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.kelvin_joule_not_commensurable : ¬PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.kelvin.Commensurable PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.jouleThe kelvin and the joule are **not** commensurable — thermodynamic temperature and energy are distinct kinds (a type-level fact).
1000398: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.iso80000_5_scale_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ (a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase).scale ≠ (b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase).scale**The scale disambiguation, on standard quantities.** There exist distinct ISO 80000-5 kinds with the same dimension `Θ` that are separated by *scale type* alone — thermodynamic temperature (ratio) and Celsius temperature (interval) witness it. Neither the dimension nor an examination principle tells them apart; the scale layer does. This is requirement R6 on the standard, the axis Parts 3 and 4 could not show.
1000397: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.iso80000_5_dim_one_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = 1**The dimension-1 disambiguation, on standard quantities.** There exist distinct ISO 80000-5 kinds with the same dimension one — the ratio of specific heat capacities and the efficiency witness it (alongside the isentropic exponent and the humidity ratios and fractions). Dimension cannot separate them; the kind layer does.
1000396: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.iso80000_5_dim_collision : ∃ a b, a.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ b.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ∧ a.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = b.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**The entropy/heat-capacity collision, on standard quantities.** There exist distinct ISO 80000-5 kinds with the same dimension `M·L²·T⁻²·Θ⁻¹` — entropy and heat capacity witness it (alongside the Massieu and Planck functions). PhysLib's `Dimension`, and any dimension-only type system, cannot separate them; the kind layer does. This is the thermodynamic dimension-does-not-classify case.
1000395: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.helmholtzEnergy_ne_gibbsEnergy : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.helmholtzEnergy.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.gibbsEnergy.kind LTMCTDimensionBase**The Helmholtz and Gibbs energies are distinct kinds — by defining construction, not by fiat.** They have the same dimension `M·L²·T⁻²` and are both "free energies", yet they are different kinds *because they are defined by different natural variables* (`A = U − TS`, natural in T,V; `G = H − TS`, natural in T,p), proved through `distinct_of_examPrinciple` (§7.5) rather than by appealing to their `id` strings. This is the thermodynamic-potential analogue of width ≠ distance and static ≠ kinetic friction force.
1000394: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.gibbsEnergy : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseGibbs energy (Gibbs function) — item 5-20.5, an energy species (`G = H − TS`, natural in T, p).
1000393: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.helmholtzEnergy : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseHelmholtz energy (Helmholtz function) — item 5-20.4, an energy species (`A = U − TS`, natural in T, V).
1000392: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.Edge : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty → PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty → PropThis application's system of energy quantities — the direct-parent edges among the thermodynamic potentials of the energy family (item 5-20).
1000391: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.helmholtzEnergy_gibbsEnergy_comparable : PropertyKindCalculus.MutuallyComparable PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.Edge (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.helmholtzEnergy.kind LTMCTDimensionBase) (PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.gibbsEnergy.kind LTMCTDimensionBase)**Mutual comparability is preserved.** The Helmholtz and Gibbs energies, though distinct kinds, remain *mutually comparable* — they share the super-kind energy, so combining them is possible but only via an explicit up-cast, never silently.
1000390: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.joulePerKelvinHeatCapacity : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe joule per kelvin **of heat capacity** (item 5-15) — *also* `M·L²·T⁻²·Θ⁻¹` and *also* written "J/K", but a unit of heat capacity, not of entropy.
1000389: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.joulePerKelvinEntropy : PropertyKindCalculus.MetrologicalUnitThe joule per kelvin **of entropy** (item 5-18) — dimension `M·L²·T⁻²·Θ⁻¹`.

1000376: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.heatCapacity : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseHeat capacity — item 5-15, dimension `M·L²·T⁻²·Θ⁻¹` (unit J/K). The heat/temperature-derivative remark is formalized in `Part5.DefiningRelations`.

1000370: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.DefiningRelations.ratio_dim_from_specific_heats : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.ratioOfSpecificHeatCapacities.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.specificHeatCapacityConstantPressure.dim LTMCTDimensionBase / PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part5.specificHeatCapacityConstantVolume.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**The ratio of specific heat capacities is dimension one because it is a ratio of two specific heat capacities.** The constant-pressure and constant-volume specific heat capacities are both `L²·T⁻²·Θ⁻¹`, so `γ = cp/cV` cancels the dimension — the ratio's dimensionlessness is a *checked computation from its defining relation*, not a stipulation. 1000364: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part4.staticFrictionForce : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseStatic friction force — item 4-9.3, a force species (pre-slip resistance).
1000363: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part4.staticFriction_ne_kineticFriction : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part4.staticFrictionForce.kind LTMCTDimensionBase ≠ PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part4.kineticFrictionForce.kind LTMCTDimensionBase**Static and kinetic friction forces are distinct kinds — by measurement principle, not by fiat.** They have the same dimension `M·L·T⁻²` and are both "friction forces", yet they are different kinds *because they are examined under different conditions* (resistance before sliding vs during sliding), proved through `distinct_of_examPrinciple` (§7.5) rather than by appealing to their `id` strings. 1000309: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.VolumeElement.volumeElement_eq_abs_det (t : Fin 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.VolumeElement.volumeElement t = |(Matrix.of fun i j => (t j).ofLp i).det|**The element is the change-of-variables volume density.** For a flat region the volume element equals `|det A|` — so `dV = |det A| du dv dw` integrates to the *actual* Euclidean volume, confirming the `√g` reading.

1000306: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.radius : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBaseRadius — item 3-1.6, a length species (centre to rim).
1000305: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.pathLength : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBasePath length (arc length) — item 3-1.7, a length species (along a curve).
1000304: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.planeAngle : PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind LTMCTDimensionBasePlane angle (angular measure) — item 3-5, dimension one, unit rad. The arc/radius remark is formalized in `Part3.DefiningRelations`.
1000303: PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.DefiningRelations.planeAngle_dim_from_arc_over_radius : PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.planeAngle.dim LTMCTDimensionBase = PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.pathLength.dim LTMCTDimensionBase / PropertyKindCalculus.Iso80000.Part3.radius.dim LTMCTDimensionBase**Under the SI's `α = s/r`, plane angle computes to dimension one.** With arc and radius taken as plain lengths, `s/r` cancels the dimension — a checked computation that reproduces the *current SI convention* rather than settling it. PKC formalizes the standard as published and leaves the dimensional stance open — plane angle nonetheless stays a distinct *kind* from every other dimension-one quantity (see `Part3.iso80000_3_dim_one_collision`), which is what keeps the radian and the steradian non-interchangeable, whatever dimension the SI ultimately assigns.

1000163: PropertyKindCalculus.InteractionAlgebra : TypeA curated **interaction algebra** over dimensioned kinds (Flater App. C). `KMul a b c` asserts the sanctioned product `a × b = c`. The relation is deliberately *partial* (most triples are absent — a category error, not a number) and *curated* (an application lists exactly the products it sanctions). The field `kMul_coherent` is the dimensional-coherence obligation R7 imposes on every edge: a sanctioned kind product must agree with the dimension layer, so the structure cannot even be formed for an algebra that violates it.

1000160: PropertyKindCalculus.Intensive.{u} {O : Type u} (k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty) (m : PropertyKindCalculus.Measurement O) : Prop**§13.5.4 intensive kind-of-quantity.** A kind `k` is *intensive* under a measurement `m` when (i) every part is measured as a value of kind `k`, and (ii) composing two parts **that already agree** leaves the value where it was: temperature, density, the angular velocity of a rigid body. Condition (ii) is Dybkær's definition read literally, and the literal reading is the design. His §13.5.4 asks that "a physical addition operation does not exist and … a quantity value is invariant with the extent of a system of constant composition" — and *of constant composition* is the clause a shorter phrasing drops. Without it the law would assert that mixing water at 20 °C with water at 80 °C leaves either reading intact. With it, agreement between the parts is the hypothesis, and what the structure says about parts that *disagree* is nothing at all: an intensive kind licenses no reading of the whole from unequal parts, which is a narrower claim than a total law and an honest one.

1000154: PropertyKindCalculus.IndividualQuantity.transpose.{u, v} {O₁ : Type u} {O₂ : Type v} {a : O₁} {b : O₂} {k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty} {R : Type} (q : PropertyKindCalculus.IndividualQuantity (a, b) k R) : PropertyKindCalculus.IndividualQuantity (b, a) k R**The transpose of a joint quantity** — the same magnitude, read as a quantity of the reversed pair. This is the equal-and-opposite reading, and it is the only re-indexing of an individual quantity this library offers. There is deliberately no general `reindex`: moving a magnitude from one object to another is exactly what the object index exists to prevent, and an operation that did it on request would return the layer to a naming convention. The transpose is safe because it is not a move — the pair `(a, b)` and the pair `(b, a)` are the same coupling read from its two ends, and which end is *source* is the whole content of a law like Newton's third. Its value is that the law becomes a type. A "reverse" that negates a magnitude and forgets to exchange the endpoints has the untransposed type, so it does not elaborate where a reversed force is expected.

1000115: PropertyKindCalculus.DimensionedKind (B : Type := LTMCTDimensionBase) [DimensionBasis B] : TypeA **dimensioned kind** (Dybkær Ch. 19): a {kind-of-property} together with the physical `Dimension` of its quantities. Pairing the dimension *with* the kind — rather than storing it on `KindOfProperty` — keeps the core spine Mathlib-free and matches the open-world convention (an application declares a dimensioned kind with a `def`, never by editing a central type). It is **parametric in the base-dimension basis** `B`: `dim` is a PhysLib `Dimension B`, so a dimensioned kind can be typed over any generating set — the SI/PhysLib default (`LTMCTDimensionBase`), Gaussian–CGS, natural units, or an angle-augmented basis. The basis parameter defaults to `LTMCTDimensionBase`, so a bare `DimensionedKind` is the familiar five-generator instance and every existing declaration reads unchanged; the parametricity is exercised where a different basis is wanted (see `DimensionExamples`). Crucially the *kind* component does not mention `B` at all: re-coordinatizing the dimension into another basis leaves the kind fixed (`DimensionedKind.extend_kind`), the formal content of the base choice living strictly *below* the kind layer.

1000111: LTMCTDimensionBase : TypePhysLib's default basis of base dimensions — `length`, `time`, `mass`, `charge`, `temperature`. Note this is *charge*-based, so it is not the SI/ISQ base-quantity set; see `Dimension`.
1000110: Dimension (B : Type) [DimensionBasis B] : TypeA dimension over a represented basis `B`. PhysLib's default basis is `LTMCTDimensionBase`.
1000108: PropertyKindCalculus.Dimension.MechanicallyReducible (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) : PropA dimension is **mechanically reducible** iff it is expressible in mass, length, and time alone — i.e. it carries no charge and no temperature exponent. This is the Finkelstein–Whitehead criterion for "*not* dimensionally independent of the four physical base units `{kg, m, s, A}`" specialized to the mechanical generators: a unit whose dimension is mechanically reducible needs neither an electromagnetic, a thermal, a luminous, nor a chemical base of its own.
1000107: ∀ {x y : O}, f x = f y → x = y
1000104: PropertyKindCalculus.Designated.ofInjective.{u, v} {O : Type u} {P : Type v} [PropertyKindCalculus.Designated P] (f : O → P) (hf : ∀ {x y : O}, f x = f y → x = y) : PropertyKindCalculus.Designated O**Designation travels along an injection.** An object type that injects into a designated one is designated: name each object by the name of its image. This is the composition principle for the whole census of object shapes — an index family, a structural object with a key, a sub-selection of a named set — and it is the only one most cases need. The injectivity hypothesis is the *author's* claim about `f`, and for a concrete finite object type it is discharged by `decide`.
1000103: PropertyKindCalculus.Designated.{u} (O : Type u) : Type u**An object type with terminological identity.** A map from the object type into the nominal `Object`, so an individual property can name the object it characterizes (§3.3) whatever the object type is. The injectivity field is the whole content of the class. Without it, an author facing a structural object type — physlib's particles, a mesh cell — can always satisfy the class by sending every object to one constant name, and the resulting designation is *worse than none*: it type-checks, it renders, and it silently reports two distinct objects as the same system. 1000052: PropertyKindCalculus.Carrier (R : Type) : Type**The numeric carrier of a quantity (R10).** The minimal *additive* structure a kind-indexed magnitude needs in order to *aggregate*: a zero and an addition, supplied once per representation type `R`. This is the role TorchLean's `Context α` plays for tensor element types — the kind, scale, dimension, interaction, and extensivity layers are all written *against* this class and reused verbatim at every `R`. **Why a bespoke `zero`/`add` rather than extending Lean's `Zero`/`Add`?** Three reasons, all deliberate: * **It is the home of additivity (extensivity §13.5, R10), nothing more.** `Carrier` carries *exactly* the operation whose laws the extensivity capstone is about. It is intentionally *not* a field/ring: multiplication and division change the *kind* (length × length = area), so they are cross-kind operations gated by `ProductKind`/`QuotientKind` witnesses, not carrier methods (see `QuantityClassification`); subtraction and the transcendentals ride Lean's own `Sub`/`MathCarrier` at their use sites. Which operations are even *meaningful* is a property of a kind's *scale* (`Scale.lean`: `AllowsOrder`/`AllowsDifference`/ `AllowsRatio`), not of the carrier — so the carrier stays minimal and the licensing lives on the kind. * **It keeps the core Mathlib-free and self-contained.** Because `add`/`zero` are bespoke methods, derived carriers — `Carrier (ι → R)` (`QuantityVector`) and `Carrier (Complex R)` (`Complex`) — are built *directly* from `R`'s `Carrier`, with no need for Mathlib's `Pi`/`Complex` algebra instances and with no risk of *instance diamonds* against them in the Mathlib-backed `dimension` layer. * **It draws the R10 line sharply** (see `LawfulCarrier`). For ergonomic *computation*, the same-kind operator `+` is also available over Lean's `Add` (see the "Two additions" note below); on any carrier that is both a `Carrier` and an `Add`, the two coincide.

These are **not** SI prefixes (the SI is decimal-only), which is why they are a separate type; but they form multiples/submultiples and bear a §1.22 conversion factor exactly as SI prefixes do — the two share the same prefixed-unit machinery.

1000040: PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty : Type**§6.19 kind-of-property** — common defining aspect of mutually comparable properties. In four-category terms (Lowe, Fig. 7.1) this is the *Attributes* corner — the non-substantial universal, instantiated by individual quantities (its modes) and characterizing sorts of system through the §20 dedicated kinds.
1000039: PropertyKindCalculus.SortOfSystem : Type**§20 sort of system** — the *sort* an object belongs to, as distinct from the object itself: *plasma* as against this plasma sample, *rover* as against rover 1, *point-particle system* as against this system of five particles. Dybkær's dedicated kind-of-property is defined over exactly this — "kind-of-property with given **sort of** system and any pertinent component" — and the neo-Aristotelian reading says why the distinction earns a carrier of its own: what parts a whole has, how they unify, and which of its quantities aggregate are facts about the *sort*, not about the individual. The mereological registry (`Composite.Assembles`) is keyed by it for that reason: volume aggregates over the parts of a rigid assembly and contracts over the parts of a mixture, and a registry keyed by the kind-of-property alone cannot say so. Specified abstractly by identity, exactly as `System` is — the two are the same shape at two ontological levels. In Lowe's four-category ontology (*The Four-Category Ontology*, 2005, Fig. 7.1) the correspondence is exact: `SortOfSystem` is the **substantial universal**, his *Kinds* corner, and `System` the **substantial particular**, his *Substances*. The other column of the square is `KindOfProperty` (his *Attributes*) over `IndividualQuantity` (his *Modes*), and the calculus carries the square's edges as well as its corners: `Sorted.sortOf` below is the left *instantiated by* edge, and the other three edges live where the corners they join are defined (`IndividualQuantity`, `DedicatedKind`). The sort is also what answers a question the mereology cannot. A decomposition of a system makes a whole out of parts without settling how many entities that whole *is*; the count comes with the sortal, under whose "individuation principle" — Marmodoro, *Whole, but not One* (2018), §4, whence "[e]very science individuates its own individual subjects or substances" — a plurality is one thing of a kind. `SortOfSystem` is where a model states its own such principle, and `Composite` (with `Assembles`) is where the statement does work.
1000037: PropertyKindCalculus.Assembles (σ : PropertyKindCalculus.SortOfSystem) (k : PropertyKindCalculus.KindOfProperty) : Prop**The aggregation license (§13.5, curated) — keyed by the sort of the whole.** A kind whose quantities may be summed over the parts of a composite *of the given sort* to give the quantity of the whole. Mass carries it for every sort a mechanical model declares; angular velocity deliberately carries it for none, and the sum of the parts' angular velocities is then not a term anyone can write. The sort index is not decoration, and the library's own counterexample is why: **volume**. Over the parts of a rigid assembly, volume aggregates; over the parts of a mixture it contracts (`mixing_subadditive` — 50 mL of ethanol and 50 mL of water make 96 mL), and both facts are facts about *volume*. A registry keyed by the kind alone must either license the mixture or refuse the assembly, and either answer is wrong. Keyed by the sort, both answers are right at once — which is the neo-Aristotelian point that how parts unify into a whole is dictated by the *sort* of the whole, not by the attribute being summed and not by the parts. Registration is opt-in — an unregistered pair has no instance and `assemble` does not elaborate — and the entry is not a formality: its `diff` field is the same scale gate `Quantity.add` demands, so a nominal or ordinal kind cannot be licensed at all. What the class does *not* prove is that the sum is the physics; that is a fact about a measurement, and `assemble_eq_measured` is where an author discharges it, per sort.

It is to the *named*, scale-checked `Quantity.add` / `Quantity.sub` what `ProductKind`/`QuotientKind` are to `Quantity.mul` / `Quantity.div`: the metrology gate, recorded in the type. (You cannot meaningfully add two *nominal* or *ordinal* quantities; this rules that out.)

1000002: List.{u} (α : Type u) : Type uLinked lists: ordered lists, in which each element has a reference to the next element. Most operations on linked lists take time proportional to the length of the list, because each element must be traversed to find the next element. `List α` is isomorphic to `Array α`, but they are useful for different things: * `List α` is easier for reasoning, and `Array α` is modeled as a wrapper around `List α`. * `List α` works well as a persistent data structure, when many copies of the tail are shared. When the value is not shared, `Array α` will have better performance because it can do destructive updates.
